'''''Eucomis zambesiaca''''' is a [[Bulb|bulbous plant]] in the family [[Asparagaceae]], subfamily [[Scilloideae]], native to southern Africa, from [[Zimbabwe]] through [[Malawi]] to the [[Limpopo|Limpopo Province]] of [[South Africa]].<ref name=WCSP_305909/> One of the smaller species in the genus,  it has a rosette of leaves about {{convert|45|cm|in|abbr=on|0}} across and  white flowers in a spike to about {{convert|30|cm|in|abbr=on|0}} tall.<ref>{{Citation |title=Eucomis Three |publisher=Pacific Bulb Society |url=http://www.pacificbulbsociety.org/pbswiki/index.php/EucomisThree |accessdate=2014-04-20 }}</ref>

==Description==
''Eucomis zambesiaca'' is a summer-growing [[Bulb|bulbous plant]] reaching about {{cvt|30|cm|ft|0}} in height when in flower. The actual bulb is relatively small, about {{cvt|3|–|5|cm|in|1}} in diameter, but is attached to an enlarged basal plate. The green leaves reach {{cvt|30|cm|ft|0}} long by {{cvt|5|cm|in|0}} wide. The sweetly scented flowers are white when they open in mid to late summer, turning green later, and are loosely arranged in a [[raceme]] on {{cvt|2|–|5|mm|in|1}} long stalks ([[Pedicel (botany)|pedicels]]). The raceme, which is variable in width, is topped by a head or "coma" of short, somewhat pointed [[bract]]s.<ref name=Comp90/><ref name=Dunc07/> The species resembles ''[[Eucomis autumnalis]]'', but this has flowers that are yellow-green rather than white when fully open and releasing pollen, angled rather than drooping pedicels, and densely packed rather than well spaced individual flowers.<ref name=Crou10/>

==Taxonomy==
''Eucomis zambesiaca'' was collected by [[John Kirk (explorer)|John Kirk]] in 1859 while accompanying [[David Livingstone]] on an expedition.<ref name=Comp90/> It was first described scientifically by [[John Gilbert Baker]] in 1886.<ref name=WCSP_305909/> ''E. zambesiaca'' is one of the mainly short, [[diploid]] species of ''Eucomis'' with 2''n'' = 2''x'' = 30 [[chromosome]]s.<ref name=ZonnDunc10/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Eucomis zambesiaca'' is native to southern Africa, from [[Zimbabwe]] through [[Malawi]] to the [[Limpopo|Limpopo Province]] of [[South Africa]].<ref name=WCSP_305909/> It is a highland species; in Zimbabwe it was found growing in short grassland at around {{cvt|1900|m|ft|-2}}.<ref name=Comp90/>

==Cultivation==
''Eucomis zambesiaca'' is grown as an [[ornamental plant]]. It has been described as "one of the prettiest species" of ''[[Eucomis]]''.<ref name=Comp90/> It has proved to be frost-hardy in the [[United Kingdom]] in well drained soil or dry sites with wall protection. It can also be grown in containers. The bulbs increase readily.<ref name=Comp90/><ref name=Dunc07/>

''E. zambesiaca'' 'White Dwarf' is a cultivar listed by the [[Royal Horticultural Society]].<ref name=RHS/> It often sold in Europe under the incorrect species name ''[[Eucomis autumnalis]]''.<ref name=VanHage/>
